# Summary Table
## Sound Frequencies
### Variables in the Replicate Frequency Table, our data missing "LAleq"
```{r}
# Define the variables of interest
variables_of_interest <- c(
  "LAFmax", "LAFmin", "LCpeak", "LAeq", "LAleq", "LCeq", "LZeq 12.5Hz", 
  "LZeq 16Hz", "LZeq 20Hz", "LZeq 25Hz", "LZeq 31.5Hz", "LZeq 40Hz", 
  "LZeq 50Hz", "LZeq 63Hz", "LZeq 80Hz", "LZeq 100Hz", "LZeq 125Hz", 
  "LZeq 160Hz", "LZeq 200Hz", "LZeq 250Hz", "LZeq 315Hz", "LZeq 400Hz", 
  "LZeq 500Hz", "LZeq 630Hz", "LZeq 800Hz", "LZeq 1kHz", "LZeq 1.25kHz", 
  "LZeq 1.6kHz", "LZeq 2kHz", "LZeq 2.5kHz", "LZeq 3.15kHz", "LZeq 4kHz", 
  "LZeq 5kHz", "LZeq 6.3kHz", "LZeq 8kHz", "LZeq 10kHz", "LZeq 12.5kHz", 
  "LZeq 16kHz", "no2"
)

# Check which variables are missing from the dataframe
missing_variables <- variables_of_interest[!variables_of_interest %in% colnames(sound_pollutant_met_data)]

# Print the missing variables
print(missing_variables)
```

### Interested Sound Frequencies
```{r}
# Define the variables of interest without LAleq
frequency_variables_of_interest <- c(
  "LAFmax", "LAFmin", "LCpeak", "LAeq",  "LCeq", "LZeq 12.5Hz", 
  "LZeq 16Hz", "LZeq 20Hz", "LZeq 25Hz", "LZeq 31.5Hz", "LZeq 40Hz",

  "LZeq 160Hz", "LZeq 200Hz", "LZeq 250Hz", "LZeq 315Hz", "LZeq 400Hz", 
  "LZeq 500Hz", "LZeq 630Hz", "LZeq 800Hz", "LZeq 1kHz", "LZeq 1.25kHz", 
  "LZeq 1.6kHz", "LZeq 2kHz", "LZeq 2.5kHz", "LZeq 3.15kHz", "LZeq 4kHz",
```

### Frequency Table
```{r}
frequency_summary_data <- data.frame(
  Variable = frequency_variables_of_interest,
  Min = NA,
  First_Qu = NA,
  Median = NA,
  Mean = NA,
  Third_Qu = NA,
  Max = NA
)

# Step 5: For the variables that exist in the dataset, calculate the summary statistics
for (var in frequency_variables_of_interest) {
  if (var %in% colnames(sound_pollutant_met_data)) {
    summary_values <- summary(sound_pollutant_met_data[[var]])
    frequency_summary_data[frequency_summary_data$Variable == var, "Min"] <- summary_values["Min."]
    frequency_summary_data[frequency_summary_data$Variable == var, "First_Qu"] <- summary_values["1st Qu."]
    frequency_summary_data[frequency_summary_data$Variable == var, "Median"] <- summary_values["Median"]
    frequency_summary_data[frequency_summary_data$Variable == var, "Mean"] <- summary_values["Mean"]
    frequency_summary_data[frequency_summary_data$Variable == var, "Third_Qu"] <- summary_values["3rd Qu."]
    frequency_summary_data[frequency_summary_data$Variable == var, "Max"] <- summary_values["Max."]
  }
}

# Step 6: Rename columns to fix the issue
colnames(frequency_summary_data) <- c("Variable", "Min", "1st Qu", "Median", "Mean", "3rd Qu", "Max")

# Step 7: Print the summary table using kable
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

table_html <- kable(frequency_summary_data, format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = F)

# Save the table as an HTML file
# save_kable(table_html, output_path("notebooks", "frequency_summary_table.html"))

```

## Pollutant
```{r}
# Define the pollutant variables of interest with descriptive names and units
pollutant_variables_of_interest <- c(
  "Methane (CH4, ppb)" = "ch4",
  "Carbon Dioxide (CO2, ppm)" = "co2_ppm",
  "Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S, ppb)" = "h2s",
  "Sulfur Dioxide (SO2, ppb)" = "so2",
  "Carbon Monoxide (CO, ppb)" = "co",
  "Ozone (O3, ppb)" = "o3",
  "Nitrogen Oxide (NOx, ppb)" = "nox",
  "Nitric Oxide (NO, ppb)" = "no",
  "Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2, ppb)" = "no2"
)

# Create a summary data frame for pollutant variables with descriptive names
pollu_summary_table <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(pollutant_variables_of_interest),
  Min = NA,
  First_Qu = NA,
  Median = NA,
  Mean = NA,
  Third_Qu = NA,
  Max = NA
)

# Calculate the summary statistics for each pollutant variable
for (desc_name in names(pollutant_variables_of_interest)) {
  var <- pollutant_variables_of_interest[[desc_name]]
  if (var %in% colnames(sound_pollutant_met_data)) {
    summary_values <- summary(sound_pollutant_met_data[[var]])
    pollu_summary_table[pollu_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "Min"] <- summary_values["Min."]
    pollu_summary_table[pollu_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "First_Qu"] <- summary_values["1st Qu."]
    pollu_summary_table[pollu_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "Median"] <- summary_values["Median"]
    pollu_summary_table[pollu_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "Mean"] <- summary_values["Mean"]
    pollu_summary_table[pollu_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "Third_Qu"] <- summary_values["3rd Qu."]
    pollu_summary_table[pollu_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "Max"] <- summary_values["Max."]
  }
}

# Rename columns to fix the issue
colnames(pollu_summary_table) <- c("Variable", "Min", "1st Qu", "Median", "Mean", "3rd Qu", "Max")

# Print the summary table using kable
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

table_html <- kable(pollu_summary_table, format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = F)

# Save the table as an HTML file
save_kable(table_html, output_path("notebooks", "pollutant_summary_table.html"))
```

## Meteorological Factor
```{r}
# Define the meteorological variables of interest with descriptive names
met_variables_of_interest <- c(
  "Wind Direction (degrees)" = "wdr_deg",
  "Wind Speed (m/s)" = "wsp_ms",
  "Temperature (F)" = "temp_f",
  "Relative Humidity (%)" = "relh_percent",
  "Solar Radiation (W/m²)" = "solr_W_m2",
  "Pressure (altitude corrected)" = "pressure_altcorr",
  "Rainfall (mm)" = "rain",
  "Water Vapor Mixing Ratio (g/kg)" = "water_vapor_mr_g_kg"
)

# Create a summary data frame for meteorological variables with descriptive names
met_summary_table <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(met_variables_of_interest),
  Min = NA,
  First_Qu = NA,
  Median = NA,
  Mean = NA,
  Third_Qu = NA,
  Max = NA
)

# Calculate the summary statistics for each meteorological variable
for (desc_name in names(met_variables_of_interest)) {
  var <- met_variables_of_interest[[desc_name]]
  if (var %in% colnames(sound_pollutant_met_data)) {
    summary_values <- summary(sound_pollutant_met_data[[var]])
    met_summary_table[met_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "Min"] <- summary_values["Min."]
    met_summary_table[met_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "First_Qu"] <- summary_values["1st Qu."]
    met_summary_table[met_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "Median"] <- summary_values["Median"]
    met_summary_table[met_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "Mean"] <- summary_values["Mean"]
    met_summary_table[met_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "Third_Qu"] <- summary_values["3rd Qu."]
    met_summary_table[met_summary_table$Variable == desc_name, "Max"] <- summary_values["Max."]
  }
}

# Rename columns to fix the issue
colnames(met_summary_table) <- c("Variable", "Min", "1st Qu", "Median", "Mean", "3rd Qu", "Max")

# Print the summary table using kable
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

table_html <- kable(met_summary_table, format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = F)

# Save the table as an HTML file
save_kable(table_html, output_path("notebooks", "met_summary_table.html"))
```

```{r}
library(ggcorrplot)

library(corrplot)

```
## Sound Frequency
```{r}
head(sound_pollutant_met_data)
```

```{r}
frequency_variables_of_interest <- c(
  "LAFmax", "LAFmin", "LCpeak", "LAeq",  "LCeq", "LZeq 12.5Hz", 
  "LZeq 16Hz", "LZeq 20Hz", "LZeq 25Hz", "LZeq 31.5Hz", "LZeq 40Hz", 
  "LZeq 50Hz", "LZeq 63Hz", "LZeq 80Hz", "LZeq 100Hz", "LZeq 125Hz", 
  "LZeq 160Hz", "LZeq 200Hz", "LZeq 250Hz", "LZeq 315Hz", "LZeq 400Hz", 
  "LZeq 500Hz", "LZeq 630Hz", "LZeq 800Hz", "LZeq 1kHz", "LZeq 1.25kHz", 
  "LZeq 1.6kHz", "LZeq 2kHz", "LZeq 2.5kHz", "LZeq 3.15kHz", "LZeq 4kHz", 
  "LZeq 5kHz", "LZeq 6.3kHz", "LZeq 8kHz", "LZeq 10kHz", "LZeq 12.5kHz", 
  "LZeq 16kHz"
)

# Step 2: Filter the dataset to include only the variables for correlation
frequency_filtered_data <- sound_pollutant_met_data[, frequency_variables_of_interest, drop=FALSE]
```

```{r}
head(frequency_filtered_data)
```

```{r warning=FALSE}
# Save the plot as a PNG file
# png(output_path("notebooks", "frequency_correlation_heatmap.png"), width = 800, height = 800)  # Set desired dimensions

# Step 1: Compute the correlation matrix
frequency_cor_matrix <- rcorr(as.matrix(frequency_filtered_data))$r  # This will calculate the Pearson correlation matrix

# Step 2: Plot the correlation matrix using corrplot with the 'circle' method
corrplot(frequency_cor_matrix, 
         method = "circle",         # Plot method
         type = "lower",            # Show only lower triangle
         col = colorRampPalette(c("red","white",  "purple"))(200),  # Custom color palette adjusted for 0-1 range
         tl.col = "black",          # Color of the text labels
         tl.cex = 0.5,              # Size of text labels
         tl.srt = 45,               # Rotation of text labels
         cl.cex = 0.8,              # Size of color legend text
         cl.lim = c(0, 1),          # Set color legend limits from 0 to 1
         addgrid.col = "grey",        
         is.corr = FALSE)           # Indicate that the matrix has no negative values

# Add a title
title("Frequency Correlation Heat Map", line = 3)  # Adjust `line` as needed

# Close the PNG device to save the file
# dev.off()
```

### Actually, there are negative correlations but at maximum of [value redacted] 
```{r}
# Find the positions of negative values in the matrix
negative_values <- which(frequency_cor_matrix < 0, arr.ind = TRUE)

# Check if there are any negative values
if (nrow(negative_values) > 0) {
  print("Negative values and their corresponding pairs (row, column):")
  for (i in 1:nrow(negative_values)) {
    row <- negative_values[i, 1]
    col <- negative_values[i, 2]
    value <- frequency_cor_matrix[row, col]
    cat("Row:", row, "Column:", col, "Value:", value, "\n")
  }
} else {
  print("All values in frequency_cor_matrix are non-negative.")
}

```

#### Question: maybe set cor < 0 to 0?
```{r}
# Set all negative values in the correlation matrix to 0
frequency_cor_matrix[frequency_cor_matrix < 0] <- 0
```

#### Corr Heat map after negative value adjustment

### Correlation Heatmap of cor >= 0.9
```{r warning=FALSE}
# Save the plot as a PNG file
#png(output_path("notebooks", "frequency_correlation_greater_0.9_heatmap.png"), width = 800, height = 800)  # Set desired dimensions

# Step 2: Set correlations below 0.9 to NA to hide them in the plot
nine_greater_matrix <- frequency_cor_matrix
nine_greater_matrix[nine_greater_matrix < 0.9] <- 0  # Only values >= 0.9 will be displayed

# Step 3: Plot the highlighted correlation matrix using corrplot
corrplot(nine_greater_matrix, 
         method = "circle",           # Use circle method
         type = "lower",              # Show only lower triangle
         col = colorRampPalette(c("white", "purple"))(200),  # Color palette for highlighted circles
         tl.col = "black",            # Text label color
         tl.cex = 0.6,                # Text label size
         tl.srt = 45,                 # Text label rotation
         cl.cex = 0.8,                # Color legend text size
         cl.lim = c(0, 1),          # Set color legend limits from 0.9 to 1
         na.label = " ",              # Hide non-highlighted cells
         addgrid.col = "grey",        
         is.corr = FALSE)             # Matrix does not contain negative values

# Add a title
title("Frequency Heat Map Highlighting Correlations ≥ 0.9", line = 3)  # Adjust `line` as needed

# Close the PNG device to save the file
#dev.off()
```

## Pearson Corr
### Sound
```{r}
frequency_variables_of_interest <- c(
  "LAFmax", "LAFmin", "LCpeak", "LAeq", "LCeq", "LZeq 12.5Hz", 
  "LZeq 16Hz", "LZeq 20Hz", "LZeq 25Hz", "LZeq 31.5Hz", "LZeq 40Hz", 
  "LZeq 50Hz", "LZeq 63Hz", "LZeq 80Hz", "LZeq 100Hz", "LZeq 125Hz", 
  "LZeq 160Hz", "LZeq 200Hz", "LZeq 250Hz", "LZeq 315Hz", "LZeq 400Hz", 
  "LZeq 500Hz", "LZeq 630Hz", "LZeq 800Hz", "LZeq 1kHz", "LZeq 1.25kHz", 
  "LZeq 1.6kHz", "LZeq 2kHz", "LZeq 2.5kHz", "LZeq 3.15kHz", "LZeq 4kHz", 
  "LZeq 5kHz", "LZeq 6.3kHz", "LZeq 8kHz", "LZeq 10kHz", "LZeq 12.5kHz", 
  "LZeq 16kHz"
)

# Step 2: Filter the dataset to include only the variables for correlation
frequency_filtered_data <- sound_low_temp_ws[, frequency_variables_of_interest, drop=FALSE]
```

```{r warning=FALSE}
# Save the plot as a PNG file
png(output_path("notebooks", "pearson_subset_frequency_correlation_heatmap.png"), width = 800, height = 800)  # Set desired dimensions

# Step 1: Compute the correlation matrix
frequency_cor_matrix <- rcorr(as.matrix(frequency_filtered_data))$r  # This will calculate the Pearson correlation matrix

# Step 2: Plot the correlation matrix using corrplot with the 'circle' method
corrplot(frequency_cor_matrix, 
         method = "circle",         # Plot method
         type = "lower",            # Show only lower triangle
         col = colorRampPalette(c("red","white",  "purple"))(200),  # Custom color palette adjusted for 0-1 range
         tl.col = "black",          # Color of the text labels
         tl.cex = 1,              # Size of text labels
         tl.srt = 45,               # Rotation of text labels
         cl.cex = 0.8,              # Size of color legend text
         cl.lim = c(0, 1),          # Set color legend limits from 0 to 1
         addgrid.col = "grey",        
         is.corr = FALSE)           # Indicate that the matrix has no negative values

# Add a title
title("Pearson Frequency Heatmap for Low Temperature(<= 70F) and\n Low Wind Speed (<= 7m/s) Conditions", cex.main = 1, line = 2)  # Adjust `line` as needed

# Close the PNG device to save the file
dev.off()
```

```{r warning=FALSE}
nine_greater_matrix[nine_greater_matrix < 0.9 & nine_greater_matrix > - 0.9] <- NA  # Only values >= 0.9 will be displayed


# Step 3: Plot the highlighted correlation matrix using corrplot
corrplot(nine_greater_matrix, 
```
```{r warning=FALSE}
         type = "lower",               # Show only lower triangle
         col = colorRampPalette(c("white", "white"))(200),  # Color palette for highlighted circles
         cl.pos = "n",
         tl.col = "black",             # Text label color
         tl.cex = 1,                 # Text label size
         tl.srt = 45,                  # Text label rotation
         cl.cex = 0.8,                 # Color legend text size
         cl.lim = c(0, 1),             # Set color legend limits
         na.label = " ",               # Hide non-highlighted cells
         addgrid.col = "grey",         # Grid color
         is.corr = FALSE,              # Matrix does not contain negative values
         addCoef.col = "black",        # Color for coefficients
         number.cex = 1,             # Font size for coefficients
         number.digits = 2)            # Display coefficients to 2 decimal places

# Add a title
```
```{r warning=FALSE}
title("Spearman Frequency Heat Map with Coefficient ≥ 0.9 for Low Temperature(> 100F) and\n Low Wind Speed (<= 7m/s) Conditions", 
      line = 2, 
      cex.main = 1)  # Adjust font size for title

# Close the PNG device to save the file
dev.off()
```
